title: The Three Cosmic Ages: From the First Man's Descent to the Dissolution of the Cosmos
arc: The teaching divides the whole spiritual drama into three discrete ages of redemption — the descent and return of the First Man, the building and standing of the cosmos by the Living Spirit and the Mother of Life, and the revealing work of the Third Ambassador down to the dissolution of the cosmos when Panaretos ascends — and then weighs their relative magnitudes to show that the first age is greatest, the third middle, and the central building-age least.
reading:
This chapter steps back from any single episode of the cosmic story and offers a survey of its whole timeline. The teaching states the bracketing measure first: from the moment when the Light came forth and was crucified in the Darkness, until the moment when Panaretos — the Last Andrias, the gathered consummating image of all redeemed light — comes up at the end, "they make three times." All redemptive time, in other words, is the time it takes for the entire Light that was mingled with the Darkness to be sifted and purified. Read correspondentially, this is the whole arc of regeneration: from the first moment Divine Truth descends into the proprium and is dispersed there as the Living Soul, until the final moment when every grain of good and truth has been separated from falsity and self-love and gathered home. Between those two limits, the work has three discrete phases.

The first age is the age of the First Man. Divine Truth descends into the realm of self-love, goes downward to the Deep, makes war and strife with the Gate of those of the Darkness and his other powers, wins the victory, and is brought back upward by the Living Spirit, the Father of Life, into the Land of Light. His sons — the Five Sons of the First Man, the five-fold Living Soul, the elements as Divine Truth in receptive form — remain below in the worlds of darkness, kept and reckoned by him so that not one should escape the hand of the Greatness. This first age corresponds to the inmost movement of redemption: the Lord's accommodation into the lowest natural for the sake of subduing the proprium, in which Divine Truth willingly becomes captive in order that nothing of what is to be saved may be lost. It is the foundational descent on which all subsequent regeneration rests, the original "purpose of heart of the Greatness" being fulfilled.

The second age opens at the very moment the First Man has come up out of the contest. Now the Living Spirit and the Mother of Life — Divine Truth in its operative, structuring power, together with Divine Wisdom in her bringing-forth — order the affairs of the cosmos and "establish it on its feet." This is the building age: the construction of the firmaments, the wheels, the luminaries, the sphere, the whole received frame within which the captive light can be processed. Read as inner process, this is the establishing of the order of regeneration itself — the fixed boundaries between states, the channels of influx, the disciplinary structures by which the mingled soul can be worked upon. It runs until the moment "they go forth from" — that is, until the cosmos is finished and the receiving frame is complete.

The third age begins when the Third Ambassador spreads forth and reveals his image. He chooses out the Light from the powers, drives the Error down into the Deep, and sets the great extracting work in motion. Sin rises against him and hides his image, and in answer Hyle paints corrupt likenesses — depicting the trees, and the abortions falling downward, and afterwards molding Adam in the flesh as the false counter-icon — until the moment Jesus the Radiance is sent, who gives heart-shape to Adam and goes up to the Height. From the Ambassador's revealing of his image until Panaretos comes up against the final clod and the cosmos dissolves: this is the third age. It is the age of extraction proper — of the awakening Call going out, the Mind of Light forming in human souls, the elect being chosen out, falsities being driven downward, and the column of redeemed light steadily ascending while the residue of unredeemed darkness gets compacted into its bolos. It ends with the dissolution of the cosmos, because once the extraction is complete the receiving frame has done its work and is no longer needed.

The teaching then turns to the relative magnitudes of these ages, and this is where its inner doctrine becomes visible. Before the cosmos stood at all, the Darkness alone was twice the length of "the two terms" together — meaning that the duration of unmingled self-love before any redemptive structure existed was greater than the duration of the building and extracting work combined. Inside the three ages, the first age, the time of the First Man, is by far the greatest; the third age, from the Ambassador's revealing to the dissolution, is "great compared with that-of-the-middle but does not approach the time of the first man"; and the second, central age in which the Father of Life and the Mother of Life formed the cosmos with its chariots, is lesser than the first. The point is not chronological curiosity. It teaches that the deepest, most costly part of redemption is the original accommodation of Divine Truth into the proprium — the silent, prolonged work of the inmost descent. The building of the receptive frame is comparatively brief, because order, once instituted from above, is laid down quickly. The extracting age, in which the Ambassador and Jesus the Radiance carry out the visible work in human history, is long but still does not approach the magnitude of that first hidden descent. A rhetorical aside addresses an interlocutor: if you say the first age is small, you will be answered that it was "greater by thirty times," while this present cosmos is small by comparison and men become only the shoot of the trees, taking many generations to bring forth fruit toward the land of sweetness.

Taken as a whole, the teaching is a doctrine of redemptive time. It tells the reader that the present world, with all its visible struggle between Light and Darkness, sits inside a much larger arc that began before the cosmos was built and will end when the cosmos is dissolved; that within this arc there are three discrete phases corresponding to descent, structuring, and extraction; and that the inmost and longest of these is the hidden labor of Divine Truth in the Deep, of which the orderly building of the cosmos and the ongoing work of awakening through the Ambassador and the Radiance are the briefer, derivative phases. Regeneration in any single soul recapitulates this same threefold pattern: first the inmost descent of the Lord into the proprium that no soul can see and that takes the longest interior time; then the establishing of the ordered frame of doctrine and state by which the soul is held; then the visible extracting work of the awakened Call in which falsity is driven downward, the image is chosen out, and the soul ascends as part of Panaretos when its cosmos finally dissolves.
